# Concurrent Drift Repair — Seconds Boundary and CanvasSource Fixture

The Awtsmoos renews the shared workspace while many hands move through its vessels; Awtsmoos.com therefore judges the present files by contract and evidence, not by memory of an earlier tree.

## Evidence
- Canonical movie protocol remains seconds; the 180-second acceptance movie and adapter tests confirm `duration === 180`.
- `AnimatorMovieAdapter` currently projects movie, sequence, camera, dialogue, performance, and asset timings without unit conversion, still in canonical seconds.
- `CanonicalMovieExportPlan` currently describes the incoming canonical movie as milliseconds and merely rounds values, producing `180` instead of required `180000`.
- The established adapter regression requires one and only one seconds-to-milliseconds conversion at the browser export boundary.
- The current shared video track source is MediaBunny `CanvasSource`, not `VideoSampleSource`; `frameQueue.js` now calls `videoSampleSource.add(timeSeconds, durationSeconds)` directly.
- The old frame-backpressure fixture still expects construction and closure of a `VideoSample`, so that assertion no longer describes the current source contract.

## Repair
1. Rewrite `CanonicalMovieExportPlan.js` so every incoming canonical timed value is validated as seconds and converted to integer milliseconds exactly once.
2. Preserve width/height/fps defaults, preferring explicit settings then canonical format.
3. Rewrite `frameBackpressure.test.mjs` to prove `CanvasSource.add()` receives exact seconds/duration and that `addCanvasFrame()` does not resolve before the deferred source acknowledgement.
4. Do not revert the shared CanvasSource source simply to satisfy a stale fixture.
5. Rerun the entire focused Node + Python gate before runtime.

## NEXT_ACTION
Fresh-hash the two existing files, rewrite both completely, then rerun all tests.
